description: A compliant flat-roof proposal where height, separations, and accessory rear-yard setback are covered by verified M4 rules.
Boundary-value proposal where height and separations are covered by verified rules and pass exactly.
The flat-roof rear-principal height exceeds the verified 7.0 m maximum.
Front-to-rear principal separation is below the verified 6.0 m minimum.
Accessory rear-yard setback is below the verified 3.0 m minimum.
Lane-yard setback is verified in the active Pipeline 5 GIS contract, so a proposal below 1.5 m should be rejected.
Rear-principal rear-yard setback is in the review queue, so the system must not approve it yet.

Fire access corridor WIDTH is verified (>=1.0 m) and this 0.8 m proposal fails it, so the proposal is rejected. The vertical CLEARANCE rule is correctly held in review: its only cited evidence ('clear of any projections or obstructions') does not deterministically support the fire_access_corridor family (rule_object_not_supported), so the verifier refuses to verify it rather than guess. The field disposition reflects that sound conservatism; the rejection decision is unchanged.

On a heritage lot, neither the lot-coverage limit nor the impervious-surface limit is verified for the heritage condition. In the M7 87-verified set the verified lot_coverage (burnaby_r1_036..040) and impervious_surface (burnaby_r1_041..044) rules are all conditioned on Rowhouse / Small-Scale-Multi-Unit dwelling types, not on a heritage lot, and heritage gating is symmetric (a heritage proposal only matches a heritage-conditioned rule). The matching heritage-conditioned coverage rules (burnaby_r1_005 lot_coverage <=60%, burnaby_r1_006 impervious_surface <=70%) are still held in the review queue for text-consensus and are not verified. Both fields therefore correctly defer to review and the overall decision stays needs_review rather than approving against an unverified rule. This is sound conservatism, not a false approval; the decision is unchanged from the prior gold expectation.
Positive control: every field is covered by a verified rule and passes it, so the proposal must be APPROVED. Falsifies 'the system can never approve'.
